title: Unity Developer
description: Build 2D/3D games, real-time interactive simulations, and spatial applications using the Unity Engine, C#, physics, and animation systems.

goal.objective: Develop high-performance 2D and 3D games and interactive simulations utilizing the versatile Unity engine and C# architecture.

learn.summary: Master C# for Unity, MonoBehaviour lifecycles, physics engines, Cinemachine cameras, UI Toolkit, ScriptableObjects architecture, Addressables, and profiling.

capstone_projects.title: 3D Action Platformer with Fluid Character Controller
capstone_projects.description: Develop a 3D platformer featuring responsive wall-jumping physics, dynamic camera tracking, particle systems, and particle effects.

capstone_projects.title: Procedural Dungeon Crawler with Custom Shaders
capstone_projects.description: Build a 3D isometric dungeon crawler featuring procedurally generated room layouts (BSP algorithm), dynamic lighting shaders, and an event-driven game architecture.

interview_focus: MonoBehaviour Lifecycle (Awake vs Start vs Update vs FixedUpdate)
Optimizing Draw Calls (Static/Dynamic Batching, GPU Instancing)
Garbage Collection Spikes Mitigation in Unity

tree.name: Unity & C# Fundamentals
tree.description: Master the foundational C# programming concepts and Unity Editor workflow essential for game development, laying the groundwork for creating interactive experiences.

resources.title: Unity Learn: Get Started with Unity

children.name: C# Programming Essentials for Unity
children.description: Learn core C# syntax including data types, variables, operators, control flow, functions, basic data structures (arrays, lists, dictionaries), delegates, and events, as directly applied in Unity scripting.

resources.title: Introduction to C# in Unity - Unity Docs

children.name: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in C#
children.description: Understand core OOP concepts: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation, abstraction, interfaces, and abstract classes, and effectively apply them in Unity game architecture and component design.

children.name: Unity Editor Interface & Workflow
children.description: Navigate the Unity Editor, understand its key windows (Scene, Game, Inspector, Project, Hierarchy), manage project settings, asset import pipelines, and establish an efficient scene setup workflow.

resources.title: Unity Editor Interface Overview - Unity Manual

children.name: GameObjects, Components & Prefabs
children.description: Understand the GameObject-Component architecture, how to add/remove components, and create reusable Prefabs for efficient scene management, modularity, and rapid prototyping.

children.name: Transforms & Coordinate Systems
children.description: Master position, rotation, and scale of GameObjects. Understand local versus world space, pivot points, and the role of parent-child hierarchies in spatial relationships.

children.name: Scripting Essentials & MonoBehaviour Lifecycle
children.description: Write basic Unity scripts, understand the MonoBehaviour lifecycle (Awake, Start, Update, FixedUpdate, LateUpdate, OnEnable, OnDisable), and handle events and interactions.

resources.title: Order of execution for event functions - Unity Docs

children.name: Version Control for Game Development
children.description: Set up Git for Unity projects, understand `.gitignore` for Unity, use Git LFS for large binary assets, and apply basic branching and merging strategies for collaborative development.

resources.title: Version control with Git and Unity - Unity Manual

tree.name: Core Game Systems Development
tree.description: Develop fundamental game mechanics using Unity's built-in systems for input, physics, UI, animation, audio, cameras, and basic rendering, forming the core of any interactive experience.

children.name: Input Management
children.description: Implement player input using both the Legacy Input Manager and the modern Input System package for various devices (keyboard, mouse, gamepad, touch) and robust action maps.

children.name: Physics & Collisions
children.description: Work with Rigidbodies, Colliders (2D & 3D), Physics Materials, Joints, Raycasting, and understand collision detection and triggers for realistic and engaging interactions.

children.name: UI/UX Development with Canvas
children.description: Design and implement user interfaces using Unity's UI Canvas system, rect transforms, fundamental UI elements (buttons, sliders, text, images), and responsive layouts for various screen sizes.

resources.title: Introduction to the Canvas - Unity Docs

children.name: UI Event System & Interactions
children.description: Understand how the Event System works, handle UI events (clicks, drags, hovers, selections), implement custom UI components, and effectively integrate UI with underlying game logic.

resources.title: Unity UI Event System - Unity Manual

children.name: Animation & Visual Effects
children.description: Create character animations with the Animator and Mecanim (states, transitions, blend trees), implement keyframe animations, and use Particle Systems for dynamic visual effects.

children.name: Unity Timeline & Cinematics
children.description: Orchestrate sequences, cutscenes, and complex animations using Unity Timeline for dynamic storytelling, event sequencing, and non-linear animation control.

children.name: Audio Integration
children.description: Integrate sound effects and background music using Audio Sources, Audio Listeners, Audio Mixers, and understand spatial audio for immersive and dynamic soundscapes.

children.name: Cameras & Projections
children.description: Master different camera types, culling masks, viewports, orthographic vs. perspective projections, and camera effects for defining the player's perspective and rendering views.

children.name: Lighting & Basic Rendering
children.description: Understand basic lighting concepts (directional, point, spot lights), light modes (realtime, baked, mixed), shadows, materials, textures, and essential rendering settings to create visually appealing scenes.

children.name: Scriptable Objects for Data Management
children.description: Utilize Scriptable Objects to store and manage game data, configurations, and settings independently of scenes and GameObjects, promoting modularity, reusability, and easier iteration.

children.name: Scene Management & Data Persistence
children.description: Manage multiple scenes, load/unload scenes additively, and implement saving/loading game data using various persistence strategies (PlayerPrefs, JSON, Binary, custom solutions) for continuous gameplay.

children.name: Asset Management & Organization
children.description: Import and manage various asset types (models, textures, audio, animations), optimize asset settings, and understand asset bundles and the Addressables system for efficient content delivery.

tree.name: Advanced Game Development & Production
tree.description: Dive into performance optimization, advanced scripting architectures, AI, editor tooling, multiplayer networking, advanced rendering, robust testing, and preparing Unity projects for industry-standard deployment and live operations.

children.name: Performance Optimization & Profiling
children.description: Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks using the Unity Profiler, Frame Debugger, and deep optimization techniques for scripts, graphics (batching, culling, GPU instancing), memory management (object pooling), and physics settings.

children.name: Advanced Scripting & Design Patterns
children.description: Implement common game design patterns (e.g., Singleton, Observer, State Machine, Command, Service Locator, Factory) to create robust, maintainable, and scalable game architectures, promoting code reusability and flexibility.

children.name: Advanced C# Features
children.description: Leverage advanced C# features such as LINQ, generics, extension methods, asynchronous programming (async/await), and custom attributes for more expressive, efficient, and modern C# code in Unity.

resources.title: Asynchronous programming with async and await - Microsoft Docs

children.name: AI & Pathfinding
children.description: Implement AI behaviors using finite state machines (FSMs), behavior trees, navigation meshes (NavMesh), obstacle avoidance, and basic AI agents for believable non-player characters and game challenges.

resources.title: Behavior Trees for AI - Unity Learn

children.name: Editor Scripting & Tool Development
children.description: Extend Unity Editor functionality with custom inspectors, editor windows, property drawers, and other tools to streamline workflows, automate tasks, and improve productivity for game development.

resources.title: Editor Scripting in Unity - Catlike Coding

children.name: Multiplayer & Networking (Optional)
children.description: Explore concepts of client-server architecture, authoritative servers, state synchronization, and use Unity's Netcode for GameObjects or third-party solutions (PUN, Mirror) for robust multiplayer functionality.

children.name: Rendering Pipelines & Shader Programming (Optional)
children.description: Understand the High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP) and Universal Render Pipeline (URP), Physically Based Rendering (PBR) workflows, and learn basic shader programming with Shader Graph or HLSL for custom visual effects.

children.name: Testing & Debugging
children.description: Implement Unit Tests, Play Mode Tests, and Integration Tests to ensure code quality and game logic correctness, and master advanced debugging techniques in Unity and Visual Studio.

resources.title: Debugging C# code in Unity - Unity Docs

children.name: Build, Deployment & Distribution
children.description: Configure build settings for various platforms (PC, mobile, console, WebGL), optimize build size, implement CI/CD for automated builds, and understand distribution platforms (Steam, App Stores).

children.name: Live Operations, Analytics & Monetization
children.description: Integrate Unity Analytics to gather player data, implement Remote Config for dynamic game content, A/B testing, and understand strategies for post-launch updates, monetization (in-app purchases, ads), and community management.

resources.title: Unity Ads and In-App Purchasing - Unity Learn

tree.name: Portfolio & Career Readiness
tree.description: Translate your Unity development skills into a strong portfolio, create compelling case studies, and prepare for interviews to land a Unity Developer role.

resources.title: Unity Learn: Prepare for a Career in Games
How to create a game development portfolio - Gamedev.net

children.name: Project Planning & Documentation
children.description: Learn to create Game Design Documents (GDDs), technical design specifications, production roadmaps, and project management plans essential for organized game development.

resources.title: Writing a Game Design Document - Gamasutra

children.name: Portfolio Project Development
children.description: Conceptualize, plan, and execute polished Unity projects that specifically showcase your core skills and specific interests (e.g., a mini-game, an interactive experience, a tool, a tech demo).

resources.title: Build Your First Game - Unity Learn

children.name: Collaboration & Teamwork in Game Dev
children.description: Understand collaborative development workflows using Git, Unity Teams/Cloud, Agile methodologies (Scrum/Kanban), and effective communication strategies within a game development team.

children.name: Case Study & Demo Reel Creation
children.description: Develop concise case studies for your projects, highlighting problem, solution, technologies used, challenges, and outcomes. Create a compelling demo reel to visually showcase your best work to potential employers.

resources.title: How to make a great portfolio for game development

children.name: Interview Preparation & Job Search
children.description: Prepare for technical interviews, coding challenges, and behavioral questions specific to Unity Developer roles. Understand the game industry job market, networking strategies, and resume/CV optimization.

resources.title: Game Development Interview Questions - Unity Forum
Guide to Getting a Job in Games - Gamasutra
